title: FluidNC CNC I/O Module description
description: PROTOTYPE, first draft -- expected to grow as more real modules are added. Describes a pluggable CNC I/O Module (see http://wiki.fluidnc.com/en/hardware/cnc_io_modules) in the same terms board.schema.json uses for a board's own onboard connectors, so a module's connector-role tooling (the wizard's role pickers, active-level/NO-NC annotation, etc.) can be reused unchanged -- the only structural difference is that a module's pins are addressed by their SOCKET POSITION (module_pin: "1".."8", the same numbering board.schema.json's expansion_socket.pins already uses) rather than a real mcu_pin, since a module's actual GPIO depends entirely on which board/socket it ends up plugged into. Resolving a module's module_pin references against a specific board's module_socket pin list (mapping module_pin -> that socket's own mcu_pin) is a wizard-runtime concern, not recorded in this file. No pin-count field on either side (see the top-level module_pins description) -- a module simply lists however many pins it actually uses, starting from "1" per the wiki's own pinout guidelines ("start with I/O #1", "put the most desirable/complex features first"); a board's module_socket simply lists however many pins are physically present at that socket. Deliberately minimal for now: only the connector shapes the first few prototype modules (simple_pendant, 5v_output, passthrough, rs485) actually need are included (generic_pins, expansion_uarts, rs485_channels) -- more of board.schema.json's connector $defs (motor_socket-shaped, etc.) should be added here as real modules that need them come along (e.g. the 10V Spindle / RC Servo-BESC / Dynamixel modules), reusing board.schema.json's existing shapes as the template rather than inventing new ones.

expansion_uarts.description: Same shape/purpose as board.schema.json's expansion_uarts -- a module carrying its own UART-based sub-connector (e.g. a pendant module's RJ12 jack), except here txd_pin/rxd_pin are module_pin references, not mcu_pin. Distinct from a module that simply forwards raw pins for the BOARD's own expansion_uarts/rs485_channels to consume -- this field is for a module that has ITS OWN fixed UART protocol/baud, same as board.schema.json's own expansion_uart.

rs485_channels.description: Same shape/purpose as board.schema.json's rs485_channels -- a module that exposes a coupled tx_pin/rx_pin(/rts_pin) RS485 bus, most commonly bound to a Modbus VFD spindle, except here the pins are module_pin references, not mcu_pin. No pins_reusable_as_generic_io field (unlike board.schema.json's rs485_channel) -- that fact is about a board's own fixed circuit sharing a physical terminal between two onboard uses, which doesn't apply to a module's own dedicated, single-purpose connector.

module_pin_ref.description: Which of the plugged-in socket's own numbered pins (1-4 normally, 5-8 for the shared-bus pins per the wiki's schematic) this connector uses -- resolved against the actual board's module_socket pin list at wizard runtime, never a real mcu_pin. The special value "*" (wildcard) is reserved for a template connector meant to be instantiated once per pin the socket actually has, in socket-pin order -- see the passthrough module's own use of this and this file's top-level description. A module file mixing "*" with other real-numbered pin references in the same connector list is not currently forbidden by this schema but doesn't make sense semantically; "*" should currently only appear alone, as a module's one and only connector.

id.description: Lowercase snake_case identifier. Filename should be <id>.module.yaml, and if the module has a photo/hotspot file, those should be images/<id>_module.jpg and hotspots/<id>_module.hotspots.yaml -- the _module suffix (not present on board files' own equivalents) exists specifically so a module id and a board id can never collide in the shared hotspots/ and images/ directories.

name.description: Human-readable module name, as it's commonly known (e.g. the wiki's own product name).

form_factor.description: Optional. Names the physical footprint standard this module follows (e.g. the wiki's own 12-pin/42mm CNC I/O Module spec), purely informational -- not used for any pin/socket compatibility check at this level; that's determined entirely by which module_pin numbers this file actually references vs. which pins a given board's module_socket lists.

conditioning.description: Identical vocabulary/meaning to board.schema.json's input_profile.conditioning -- see that file for the full active-level derivation notes. A module's own conditioning circuitry is a fixed fact of the module (independent of whatever board/socket it's plugged into), exactly like a board's generic_pin conditioning is a fixed fact of the board.

module_generic_pin.description: Same shape/purpose as board.schema.json's generic_pin, with module_pin (a socket-position reference, possibly the "*" wildcard -- see module_pin_ref) in place of mcu_pin.

label.description: The module's OWN label for this connector (silkscreen/vendor documentation term), or a generic description (e.g. "Output") for a module simple enough not to have its own per-pin silkscreen label.

generic_name.description: Same purpose as board.schema.json's generic_pin.generic_name -- optional, omit to fall back to label.

module_expansion_uart.description: Same shape/purpose as board.schema.json's expansion_uart, with txd_pin/rxd_pin as module_pin references in place of mcu_pin.

module_rs485_channel.description: Same shape/purpose as board.schema.json's rs485_channel, with tx_pin/rx_pin/rts_pin as module_pin references in place of mcu_pin.

rts_pin.description: Optional -- present only if this module has a dedicated direction/driver-enable pin for the RS485 transceiver. Omit rather than guessing one (see board.schema.json's rs485_channel.rts_pin -- some transceivers wire for automatic direction sensing and have no such pin at all).
